scope: Independent backing admission for both generation-owned scheduler and completion timer-account bundles through final strong/weak/allocator release; event admission and reserve grants remain separate.

policy.dimension: fixed account Arc plus private allocation-holder bundle
policy.decision: Twice the two-account needs at complete-root capacity leaves headroom for retained generations, namespace replacement and concurrent preparation, with one quarter reserved for trusted storage. A separate pool avoids coupling idle-root lifetimes to active event admission. No existing ceiling is raised or RAM preallocated.
policy.cost: One private holder allocation per account and one extra machine word per account reference; enclosing admitted layouts reserve actual increased sizes.
policy.namespace_scope: Every fully prepared namespace owns one fresh admitted timer account, including empty namespaces. Global nodes allocated before timer-account admission and independently surviving record/CQ/watch accounts still need independent admission.

controls: Actual fixed-layout timer-account Arcs fill ordinary and total ceilings; 64 heap-held ordinary denials and total trusted denial prove reservation precedes either allocation. Account pressure does not allocate a maximum event footprint.

Ordinary namespace replacement at exhaustion rejects AllocationFailed and preserves the original account. Failed root registration returns MemorySponsorAllocationFailed with exact frame/root/account recovery before ASID publication.

Trusted root and completion namespace construction at ordinary exhaustion consume only trusted backing. A scheduler event reservation and actual completion timer submission still consume ordinary event admission until an explicit platform grant.

Late promotion does not reclassify either original root/namespace account. Closing that root at total exhaustion refunds both ordinary slots, and fresh root plus namespace publication/close recovers exactly.

Actual prepared event/node/cancellation backing retains its scheduler account across root close and exact ASID reuse. Node disposal retains event admission with the cancellation handle; handle release ends event admission, while a weak account still retains backing until final weak release. The successor remains unaffected.

Completion namespace replacement/close separately retains its timer-account backing after final strong release until weak release. Five preparation-stage errors restore unused account admission; 64 fresh heap/account-pool-held publications/removals enter neither allocator nor account pool.

Existing actual root-account partial parent fallback retains one timer account under lifecycle/root/ledger/heap/root-metadata/waiter-account/timer-account pool guards. Existing unpublished CQ namespace and detached retired namespace fallback controls retain one original account each under heap/registry/account-pool guards; no additional deliberate-retention fixture was added.
Shared allocation-owner host controls inject holder/payload failure, check phase abandonment, single-allocation allowance, clone/final-weak concurrency and deallocation before refund.
qualification_limits: Fixed-bundle counts do not account for exact heap bytes, allocator overhead or aggregate principal/general-heap consumption.

Native pressure allocates actual accounts. Native scheduler lifetime control owns a real prepared, never-enqueued event and cancellation state. Shared host controls inject allocation failures; native heap exhaustion is not forced.
Completion/CQ/watch account backing, Waker/callback/other observer storage and remaining registry metadata still need admission. SEC-07 remains partial.

No sustained hostile concurrent EL0 backing-pressure fairness, per-service progress entitlement, worst-case lookup/IRQ latency or physical hardware qualification. Existing C03/C16/C18 and G1/G4 outer-context/destructor limits remain; no new cleanup or retry authority.
